 Giri, Firouzja Advance To Final Match
 NM
 AnthonyLevin
 Updated: Nov 18, 2026, 6:03 PM
 | 
 58 
 | 
 Chess Event Coverage
 GMs Alireza Firouzja and Anish Giri won their matches to advance to the Knockout 1 Final in the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot 2026 . GM Fabiano Caruana won the second set against Firouzja (including a fast classical win), but the French number-one won the match in armageddon. Giri, on the other hand, won the second set against GM Maxime Vachier-Lagrave —in addition to the first—and avoided the tiebreak altogether.
 Day nine starts on Thursday, November 19, at 9 a.m. ET / 15:00 CET / 7:30 p.m. IST .
 Knockout 1: Smooth Sailing For Giri, Firouzja Edges Out Caruana 
 Knockout 2: Niemann, Duda In Final 
 Knockout 3: Arjun, Martirosyan In Final 
 Knockout 4: Aronian, So In Final 
 Knockout 5: Carlsen, Artemiev In Final 
 Knockout 6: Praggnanandhaa, Mishra In Final 
 Day two of the Knockout concluded the first set of matches, producing a Final and a Consolation Match in every bracket. As mentioned earlier, the slate was wiped clean and the players again contested four blitz games (3+2), two rapid games (15+10), and one fast classic game (45+30).
 The winner earned one "set point" per day, regardless of the margin of their victory, and two set points won the match. In the event of a 1-1 tie—as in Firouzja vs. Caruana, where Firouzja won day one and Caruana won day two—an armageddon game settled the score.
 Firouzja wins in armageddon. Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess. 
 Keep reading, but you can also check out GM Hikaru Nakamura 's recap video below.
 Knockout 1: Smooth Sailing For Giri, Firouzja Edges Out Caruana
 The two players who led after Tuesday won their respective matches on Wednesday. For Giri, the road was less complicated; he won both sets without a single loss. On the second day, he won one blitz game and one rapid game, while making draws in all the others.
 After the match, he said: "Maxime is obviously a much better player in this type of format, in rapid and blitz, quick chess. I was quite fortunate, played well for my standards, and managed to overcome." As for the Final, he said, "Maybe I'll get lucky!"
 Maxime is obviously a much better player in this type of format. 
 —Anish Giri
 Giri interviewed after the game. Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess. 
 Giri held his own in the blitz portion, winning game three. With the black pieces in the Reti Opening, he neutralized an aggressive attempt with 7.Ne5 , reached an equal endgame, and capitalized at once on the opportunity to double his opponent's pawns. Vachier-Lagrave must have underestimated the simple-looking 21...Bxc3! , after which the engine claims White is strategically lost.
 --> 
 With set one in the pocket and a point ahead, "don't lose" was the name of the game. And Giri did just that. He was on the better side of a draw in the first rapid game, and then picked up four points in the second rapid game, with the white pieces. The opening didn't go well for Vachier-Lagrave, as he gave Giri the best possible version of a thematic pawn sacrifice in the Queen's Indian Defense. It's not even "just compensation" in this case—White won his pawn back pretty quickly.
 --> 
 Giri confessed that taking a draw with a better position in the fast classic game was a "sin," but it did win him the match. Perhaps he can be forgiven.
 As for the other match, there was just one draw in Firouzja vs. Caruana. Firouzja won the first three blitz games but lost the fourth; then, they made a draw and Caruana won a rapid game. In a must-win fast classic game with the black pieces, Firouzja self-destructed and lost the set.
 Both players won a set, and it was Firouzja who won the armageddon tiebreak.
 Firouzja nearly managed to repeat the 4-0 sweep in blitz, but fell one game short. The three points he earned in blitz, however, were negated by Caruana's one win in rapid, which is worth four points. After the match, Firouzja said that the only thing he'd change about the format is the value of blitz games.
 Speaking about the points system as well, GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov (in the sixth bracket) felt that four points for a rapid game was too much. 
 "I think everything other than the blitz point system is good, but on the blitz point system it's really not fair that I won three games and after I lose one game in rapid you're down in the match." - Alireza Firouzja after winning the match in armageddon https://t.co/ameE5L3Z5k 
— chess24 ( @chess24com ) November 18, 2026 
 The rapid portion started with a Classical Sicilian (Caruana with White), but the queens got traded and we saw an accurate draw, 98 accuracy by both sides. Game two, an Exchange French, was decisive. With Black in the time scramble, Caruana used his two-minute time advantage (Firouzja on 16 seconds) to find the winning counterblow 38...Rc2! .
 --> 
 After that, Caruana won convincingly in the fast classic game, where Firouzja played the unusual 2...Qa5 against the Alapin Sicilian to generate winning chances. With this win, Caruana has a 2794 classical rating—seven points under Carlsen. GM Rafael Leitao analyzes the Game of the Day.
 --> 
 The match was even at 1-1 after this game, and Firouzja won the armageddon. Caruana lost his a-pawn and the position collapsed—or, in  GM David Howell 's words, "The black position is cooked."
 In David Howell's grandmaster opinion, if Caruana doesn't find a way to stop Bxb7 and a6-a7, "the black position is cooked"! https://t.co/HEJcaXJn6m #TotalChess https://t.co/zed3rT78RG 
— chess24 ( @chess24com ) November 18, 2026 
 Giri will face Firouzja in the Final, while Caruana and Vachier-Lagrave will contest third place. 
 Knockout 2: Niemann, Duda In Final
 In the second knockout bracket, GM Hans Niemann and GM Jan-Krzysztof Duda defeated GMs Liem Le and Ian Nepomniachtchi . Niemann won both sets, while Duda won a nailbiter armageddon game.
 Niemann convincingly defeated the former world number-14. Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess. 
 Niemann won convincingly, with one win and two losses in blitz, a win in rapid, and finally a win in fast classic. Ahead of the final game, with a three-point lead, he had one goal: "Not losing."
 Q: "Anything specific you want to focus on going into the classical game?" Hans: "Not losing." #TotalChess https://t.co/3OmBq8IBDU 
— chess24 ( @chess24com ) November 18, 2026 
 He equalized comfortably in a Closed Catalan and went on to win when Le overpressed. The rook coming down on the c-file made greater threats than its counterpart on the a-file.
 --> 
 After losing the first set on Tuesday, Duda came back from behind to turn the match around. He won the second set with two wins and a loss in blitz, a trade of wins in rapid, and finally a win in fast classic.  With a 1-1 score, it was a thriller armageddon that won the Polish grandmaster the match.
 Nepomniachtchi had a seven-to-two-minute time advantage, with no increment for another 17 moves. At precisely this moment, WIM Fiona Steil-Antoni foreshadowed, "It feels like unless Ian Nepomniachtchi blunders something big, this is going to be such an uphill battle against the clock," one breath before Nepomniachtchi hung a pawn.
 Duda wins an extremely close fight. Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess. 
 The game went downhill from there, but Duda still had to win the game with seconds on the clock. He managed to reach move 41 and play on the increment, but barely. Duda called it "a lucky game," saying that he would have lost if the increment had started after move 60 instead.
 The video of the game is more appropriate for the drama than game annotations. 
 Duda wins an incredibly nervous game on the increment and advances to the Knockout 2 Final against Hans Niemann! #TotalChess https://t.co/J5ItlxIeQ3 
— chess24 ( @chess24com ) November 18, 2026 
 Nepomniachtchi and Le will still return on Thursday to contest the consolation match.
 Knockout 3: Arjun, Martirosyan In Final
 In the third bracket, GM Arjun Erigaisi beat GM Jorden van Foreest in armageddon, while GM Haik Martirosyan beat GM Richard Rapport 2-0.
 Rapport was one of three players not to show up to the fast classic game, along with GMs Magnus Carlsen (again) and Abhimanyu Mishra . In each case, it did not change the outcome of the match; Rapport would have lost anyway, while Carlsen and Mishra won their matches with a game to spare.
 It may be easier for the winner of the match to say, but Martirosyan commented that he would probably never skip a game. "I thought it's good to play chess anyway," he said. "I'm very happy when I am next to the chessboard, but maybe one day if I will be so tired—but I don't think I will do it." He was also full of praise for Rapport: "I played such an interesting, such a fantastic player... I was enjoying [it] because of my opponent's style."
 I thought it's good to play chess anyway. 
 —Haik Martirosyan
 Rapport doesn't show up. Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess. 
 Knockout 4: Aronian, So In Final
 GMs Levon Aronian and Wesley So have set up an all-American Final in the fourth bracket.
 At the start of the day, So entered the confessional booth to publicly apologize for his negative statements about the tournament and its format. He brought notes for the apology, which started with, "I think I was wrong." You can listen to the rest of it in the post below.
 Wesley So: "I think I was wrong. I would like to take this time to sincerely apologize for the way I criticized the Total Chess tournament and its format." "I think I was out of place and I should really just stop b****ing." #TotalChess https://t.co/GCQtiJdQ5B 
— chess24 ( @chess24com ) November 18, 2026 
 Knockout 5: Carlsen, Artemiev In Final
 Carlsen and GM Vladislav Artemiev are in the Final. As stated above, Carlsen didn't show up to this game either, and a draw would have sent him under the 2800 rating for the first time in 17 years. He had already clinched his match against GM Bibisara Assaubayeva .
 It remains a question: will we see him play a fast classic game against Artemiev?
 Carlsen not at the board. Photo: Maria Emelianova/Total Chess. 
 Knockout 6: Praggnanandhaa, Mishra In Final
 GMs Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu and Mishra are through to the Final. In a funny twist, Praggnanandhaa quipped he was more relieved to avoid playing his sister than he was to win the match. Had he lost against Abdusattorov, he would have played the Consolation Match against GM Vaishali Rameshbabu .
 After skipping the fast classic game and winning anyway, Mishra addressed criticism by the CEO of FIDE Enterprises, GM Emil Sutovsky , in an X post . He explained that he was exhausted after seven games a day and that he also received permission from the chief arbiter not to show up to the game. He added that he was still unclear on whether the games would be classically rated or not, if the match was already won.
 "Given that uncertainty, combined with the fatigue I felt, plus permission from the chief arbiter, I had sufficient reasons not to show up," he wrote.
 Mishra took the option of not showing up. Photo: Maria Emelianova/Total Chess. 
 With two days left, we are near the end of a long tournament. But one thing's for sure: nobody gets a break! Thursday and Friday feature the last matches, with seven games a day.
 How to watch? 
 You can watch the event on the Chess24 Twitch or YouTube pages, or on GM Hikaru Nakamura 's Kick channel . You can find the games on our dedicated events page .
 The live broadcast was hosted by GM David Howell , IMs Jovanka Houska and Anna Rudolf , and WIM Fiona Steil-Antoni .
 The Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot 2026 takes place on November 10-21 at the Anantara New York Palace Hotel in Budapest, Hungary. The event is a trial run for the official event in 2027, which will crown the first FIDE World Combined Champion. The event consists of a round-robin group stage and a knockout combining blitz, rapid, and fast classical time controls. The time control is 3+2 for blitz, 15+10 for rapid, 45+30 for fast classical, and 10 minutes (White) vs. 7 minutes (Black) with a one-second increment starting on move 41 in armageddon.
